editorial: During the war in Afghanistan you’ll feel the grit of an interpreter carrying a wounded sergeant across impossible miles, and every frame breathes that pressure. Its low key pacing mirrors a soldier’s slowed heartbeat, pulling you into an almost meditative dread that grips before the action pivots. A sluggish midsection does test your patience, but the film’s relentless authenticity pulls you back. Joaquin Phoenix delivers a nearly silent performance that anchors the film’s claustrophobic gravity, turning every look into a silent conversation. Ideal for those who crave intimate character driven war dramas that linger long after the credits.
targetAudience: Ideal for those who crave intimate, character-driven war dramas that linger long after the credits.
